issues.legal_issue: A preliminary authorization for depositing title deeds requires registration only if it forms an integral part of the written bargain creating security over immovable property.
material_facts: The authorization permitted a representative to deposit title deeds to secure advances, but did not state the principal amount borrowed or to be borrowed, the interest rate, or the details of the deeds to be deposited.
The court found that the authorization was not intended to form an integral part of the transaction and did not itself create an interest in the property.
issues.conclusion: The authorization was merely evidential and did not require registration.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 58(f) of the Transfer of Property Act, a mortgage by deposit of title deeds is created when title deeds are delivered with intent to create security. Ordinarily, the law implies the mortgage contract from the deposit and intent. If the parties reduce their bargain about the security to writing, that written bargain is the sole evidence of its terms and requires registration under Section 17 of the Registration Act if it creates an interest in immovable property; Section 59 does not otherwise require a registered instrument for this form of mortgage. The distinction between a written bargain and a memorandum that merely records or evidences a transaction is supported by Kedarnath Dutt v. Shamloll Khettry, Pranjivandas Mehta v. Chan Ma Phee, Shaw v. Foster, Obla Sundarachariar v. Narayana Ayyar, and Rachpal Mahraj v. Bhagwandas Daruka.

rule.if: appeal_from_denial_of_mortgage_decree and preliminary_authorization_for_title_deposit and authorization_omits_loan_amount and authorization_omits_interest_rate and authorization_omits_deed_details

predicates.appeal_from_denial_of_mortgage_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from the denial of a mortgage decree.
predicates.preliminary_authorization_for_title_depo: A written authorization permits another person to deposit title deeds as security for advances.
predicates.authorization_omits_loan_amount: The authorization does not state the amount borrowed or to be borrowed.
predicates.authorization_omits_interest_rate: The authorization does not state the interest rate for the loan.
predicates.authorization_omits_deed_details: The authorization does not identify the title deeds to be deposited.

issues.definition: When an appeal from the denial of a mortgage decree concerns a preliminary authorization for depositing title deeds that omits the loan amount, interest rate, and deed details, the authorization does not require registration.

issues.legal_issue: A letter authorizing further negotiation about title deeds and a later record of an already completed deposit do not require registration when neither is the written bargain creating the security.
material_facts: One letter authorized a representative to deliver title deeds and negotiate further, omitted material loan particulars and details of the deeds, and indicated that the transaction had not yet been finally completed.
A later letter stated that the title deeds had been deposited with intent to create a mortgage, but recorded a transaction whose rights and liabilities had already been agreed upon.
The later letter was written by a person who was not the head of the family, and its language referred to the writer's own rights, title, and interest in the properties.
issues.conclusion: Neither letter was an integral part of the bargain creating the security, and neither required registration.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17 of the Registration Act requires registration when the parties intend a document itself to embody the bargain creating an interest in immovable property. A document that merely evidences a concluded deposit transaction does not require registration. The court applied the distinction stated in Pranjivandas Mehta v. Chan Ma Phee and Shaw v. Foster, and relied particularly on Rachpal Mahraj v. Bhagwandas Daruka in treating a record of an already concluded transaction as evidential rather than operative.

predicates.appeal_from_denial_of_mortgage_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from the denial of a mortgage decree.
predicates.title_deposit_letter_authorizes_further_: A letter concerning delivery of title deeds authorizes further negotiation about the arrangement.
predicates.title_deposit_letter_omits_material_loan: That letter omits material loan particulars and details of the title deeds.
predicates.deposit_record_describes_completed_trans: A later document records a deposit transaction whose rights and liabilities had already been agreed upon.
predicates.deposit_record_does_not_itself_create_se: The later document records the deposit rather than itself embodying the bargain that creates the security.

issues.definition: In an appeal from the denial of a mortgage decree, a title-deposit letter authorizing further negotiation and omitting material details, or a document merely recording a completed deposit, does not require registration.

issues.legal_issue: A mortgage decree may be granted where title deeds are deposited with intent to secure repayment and the accompanying letters merely authorize or record the deposit rather than embody the written bargain creating the mortgage.
material_facts: The title deeds to the properties were deposited at the bank's head office with the stated intent to create an equitable mortgage securing repayment of money owed or later becoming owed.
The authorization and related letters did not constitute the written bargain creating the security and did not require registration.
The suit sought recovery of the debt with enforcement against the mortgaged properties.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed and a mortgage decree was granted, with the mortgaged properties to be sold if the debt was not paid within the time specified in the decree.
issues.legal_principle: Section 58(f) of the Transfer of Property Act recognizes a mortgage by deposit of title deeds in the specified towns when the debtor delivers title deeds to the creditor with intent to create security. Where the deposit and intent establish the mortgage and no operative written bargain requiring registration exists, the mortgage can be enforced. The court granted the usual mortgage decree under Order 34, Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

rule.if: appeal_from_denial_of_mortgage_decree and title_deeds_delivered_to_creditor and delivery_made_in_recognized_location and delivery_intended_as_security and accompanying_documents_not_written_security_bargain

predicates.appeal_from_denial_of_mortgage_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from the denial of a mortgage decree.
predicates.title_deeds_delivered_to_creditor: The debtor delivered title deeds to the creditor or the creditor's agent.
predicates.delivery_made_in_recognized_location: The title deeds were delivered in a location where this form of mortgage is recognized.
predicates.delivery_intended_as_security: The delivery was made with the intent to secure repayment of the debt.
predicates.accompanying_documents_not_written_secur: The accompanying documents merely authorize or record the deposit and do not themselves embody the written bargain creating the security.

issues.definition: When a mortgage-decree appeal concerns title deeds delivered to a creditor in a recognized location with intent to secure repayment, and the accompanying documents are not the written security bargain, a mortgage decree is granted.
